metadata.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

nodes.name: BERT model architecture
nodes.statement: BERT's model architecture is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder based on the original implementation described in \citet{vaswani-etal:2017:_atten} and released in the {\tt tensor2tensor} library.

nodes.name: Model notation ($L$, $H$, $A$)
nodes.statement: In this work, we denote the number of layers (i.e., Transformer blocks) as $L$, the hidden size as $H$, and the number of self-attention heads as $A$.

nodes.name: ``sentence'' and ``sequence''
nodes.statement: Throughout this work, a ``sentence'' can be an arbitrary span of contiguous text, rather than an actual linguistic sentence. A ``sequence'' refers to the input token sequence to BERT, which may be a single sentence or two sentences packed together.

nodes.name: WordPiece embeddings
nodes.statement: We use WordPiece embeddings \cite{wu-etal:2016:_googl} with a 30,000 token vocabulary.

nodes.name: Input representation vectors ($E$, $C$, $T_i$)
nodes.statement: we denote input embedding as $E$, the final hidden vector of the special {\tt [CLS]} token as $C \in \mathbb{R}^{H}$, and the final hidden vector for the $i^{\rm th}$ input token as $T_i \in \mathbb{R}^H$.

nodes.name: Masked LM (MLM)
nodes.section: BERT — Pre-training BERT — Task #1: Masked LM
nodes.statement: In order to train a deep bidirectional representation, we simply mask some percentage of the input tokens at random, and then predict those masked tokens. We refer to this procedure as a ``masked LM'' (MLM), although it is often referred to as a {\it Cloze} task in the literature~\cite{taylor:1953:_cloze}. In this case, the final hidden vectors corresponding to the mask tokens are fed into an output softmax over the vocabulary, as in a standard LM. In all of our experiments, we mask 15\% of all WordPiece tokens in each sequence at random. In contrast to denoising auto-encoders \cite{vincent:2008}, we only predict the masked words rather than reconstructing the entire input.

nodes.name: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)
nodes.section: BERT — Pre-training BERT — Task #2: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP)
nodes.statement: In order to train a model that understands sentence relationships, we pre-train for a binarized {\it next sentence prediction} task that can be trivially generated from any monolingual corpus. Specifically, when choosing the sentences {\tt A} and {\tt B} for each pre-training example, 50\% of the time {\tt B} is the actual next sentence that follows {\tt A} (labeled as {\tt {\small IsNext}}), and 50\% of the time it is a random sentence from the corpus (labeled as {\tt {\small NotNext}}).

nodes.name: Masking Procedure
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 — Masked LM and the Masking Procedure
nodes.statement: Assuming the unlabeled sentence is {\tt {\small my dog is hairy}}, and during the random masking procedure we chose the 4-th token (which corresponding to {\tt {\small hairy}}), our masking procedure can be further illustrated by \begin{itemize} \item 80\% of the time: Replace the word with the {\tt [MASK]} token, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is [MASK]}} \item 10\% of the time: Replace the word with a random word, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is apple}} \item 10\% of the time: Keep the word unchanged, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is hairy}}. The purpose of this is to bias the representation towards the actual observed word. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: 80% -> [MASK] token
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 — Masked LM and the Masking Procedure
nodes.statement: 80\% of the time: Replace the word with the {\tt [MASK]} token, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is [MASK]}}

nodes.name: 10% -> random word
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 — Masked LM and the Masking Procedure
nodes.statement: 10\% of the time: Replace the word with a random word, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is apple}}

nodes.name: 10% -> unchanged word
nodes.section: Appendix A.1 — Masked LM and the Masking Procedure
nodes.statement: 10\% of the time: Keep the word unchanged, e.g., {\tt {\small my dog is hairy $\rightarrow$ my dog is hairy}}. The purpose of this is to bias the representation towards the actual observed word.

nodes.name: GLUE classification loss
nodes.statement: The only new parameters introduced during fine-tuning are  classification layer weights $W \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times H}$, where $K$ is the number of labels. We compute a standard classification loss with $C$ and $W$, i.e., $\log({\rm softmax}(CW^T))$.

nodes.name: SQuAD answer-span scoring
nodes.statement: The probability of word $i$ being the start of the answer span is computed as a dot product between $T_i$ and $S$ followed by a softmax over all of the words in the paragraph: $P_i = \frac{e^{S{\cdot}T_i}}{\sum_j e^{S{\cdot}T_j}}$. The analogous formula is used for the end of the answer span. The score of a candidate span from position $i$ to position $j$ is defined as  $S{\cdot}T_i + E{\cdot}T_j$, and the maximum scoring span where $j \geq i$ is used as a prediction. The training objective is the sum of the log-likelihoods of the correct start and end positions.

nodes.name: SQuAD 2.0 null-span scoring
nodes.statement: We treat questions that do not have an answer as having an answer span with start and end at the {\tt [CLS]} token. The probability space for the start and end answer span positions is extended to include the position of the {\tt [CLS]} token. For prediction, we compare the score of the no-answer span: $s_{\tt null} = S{\cdot}C + E{\cdot}C$ to the score of the best non-null span $\hat{s_{i,j}}$ =  $ {\tt max}_{j \geq i} S{\cdot}T_i + E{\cdot}T_j$. We predict a non-null answer when  $\hat{s_{i,j}} > s_{\tt null} + \tau $, where the threshold $\tau$ is selected on the dev set to maximize F1.

nodes.name: Next Sentence Prediction examples
nodes.statement: The next sentence prediction task can be illustrated in the following examples. \begin{align*} \text{Input\;} &= \text{\tt {\scriptsize [CLS] the man went to [MASK] store [SEP]}} \\ & \text{\tt {\scriptsize \;\;\;\;\;\;\;he bought a gallon [MASK] milk [SEP]}}\\ \text{Label} &= \text{\tt {\scriptsize IsNext}} \\ \\ \text{Input\;} &= \text{\tt {\scriptsize [CLS] the man [MASK] to the store [SEP]}}\\ &\text{\tt {\scriptsize \;\;\;\;\;\;\;penguin [MASK] are flight \#\#less birds [SEP]}}\\ \text{Label} &= \text{\tt {\scriptsize NotNext}} \end{align*}
